content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and art director for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown ONE small enemy sprite,
at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right), on a neutral grey-blue background
that is not part of the sprite.

The sprite is supposed to be this enemy:
"A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
Intended size: about 16x16 to 20x20 px. Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether it is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy that matches the description. Be calibrated:
authentic Capcom enemy sprites score about 90-95; competent fan art about 60-70; amateur or AI-looking pixel art
about 30-45. Do not reward or punish a sprite for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- authenticity: could ship unchanged in MM2/MM3 (Capcom conventions, not "modern pixel art")
- description_fidelity: matches the description (body, features, role)
- readability_1x: the silhouette and features read instantly at true size
- pixel_craft: 1-px black outlines used the Capcom way, clean clusters, no jaggies, orphans, dithering or noise
- palette_discipline: NES colours, flat shading with at most one highlight, about 3 colours + transparent per 8x8 tile
- appeal: charm and character in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"authenticity": n, "description_fidelity": n, "readability_1x": n, "pixel_craft": n,
  "palette_discipline": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"authenticity":3,"description_fidelity":3,"readability_1x":4,"pixel_craft":4,"palette_discipline":5,"appeal":4},"score":39,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["At 1x the diagonal silhouette reads more like a rocket, fish, or drill than a floating Blooper-like squid.","The lower-left section forms one striped taper instead of a clear group of tentacles gathered for thrust.","The large upper-right red-and-black block overwhelms the body and has no clear squid anatomy or mechanical function.","Only one small eye is legible; the warning-eyes concept and expressive Mega Man-style face are not communicated.","The outline varies from 1 px to heavy black wedges, especially around the right and underside, obscuring the form.","Red and white pixels alternate in choppy stair-step clusters along the lower body, creating checkerboard noise rather than intentional flat shading.","The sprite uses black, white, red, and salmon within a compact area, making the NES tile palette discipline questionable.","The pose lacks the compact symmetry, clean silhouette, and toy-like charm typical of Mega Man 2-3 small enemies."],"fixes":["Rebuild the body as a compact 12-14 px rounded or bell-shaped squid head, with the propulsion direction expressed by animation rather than a long diagonal taper.","Replace the lower-left striped tail with three or four distinct 1-2 px tentacle tips separated by clean negative-space notches.","Use a consistent 1 px black contour and remove the broad black masses at the upper-right and underside.","Give the face two readable eye sockets or a clearly designed side-view eye assembly; reserve bright red pixels for the pre-explosion flash frame.","Consolidate interior colors into large clusters: one main body color, one highlight color, and black, avoiding alternating red-white staircase pixels.","Reduce or remove the salmon shade so each 8x8 region stays near three opaque colors plus transparency.","Create two animation poses: tentacles tucked tightly beneath the body, then tentacles flared backward by 2-3 px for the thrust pulse.","Square off accidental jaggies and isolated pixels so every protrusion describes either the shell, eye housing, or a specific tentacle."]}
